conventions.choice: One Kekule/Lewis structure per file with integer bond orders, explicit hydrogens, explicit lone-pair counts and formal charges. Octet-obeying forms are used wherever one exists (SO2, HCO3-, zwitterion carboxylates); expanded valence shells only where unavoidable (SF6, PCl5, XeF4); BF3 keeps an incomplete octet (three single bonds, no B=F).
conventions.why: Matches OpenStax Chemistry 2e 7.3/7.4/8.3. The validator formula (valence - lone-pair electrons - sum of bond orders) reproduces every stored formal charge.

conventions.choice: RECOMMENDED: octet-obeying resonance form. S1 (formal charge +1, one lone pair) double-bonded to O1 (two lone pairs, 0) and single-bonded to O2 (three lone pairs, -1). Both S-O bonds carry the resonance note (effective order 1.5). S: oxidation state +4, steric number 3, bent, sp2.
conventions.why: OpenStax Chemistry 2e Example 8.4 draws exactly these two resonance structures (verified from the figure description: S with one lone pair and a positive sign, single-bonded O with three lone pairs and a negative sign, the other O double-bonded). The Purdue/Bodner general chemistry review also presents SO2 as two resonance structures differing in which O holds the double bond. The alternative (O=S=O, zero formal charges, 10 electrons on S) is the "minimise formal charge" convention that texts such as Brown et al. apply to sulfate; it gives the same oxidation state (+4), steric number (3), geometry (bent) and hybridization (sp2), so only the stored bond orders, lone pairs, formal charges and the resonance note differ. The octet form is preferred because it predicts the observed equal S-O bonds via resonance without invoking d orbitals, and it is what the cited open textbook shows. Verification addendum: the competing O=S=O convention is shown for SO2 itself in a McMaster University general chemistry lecture slide (source mcmaster-chem1a3-so2), and PubChem CID 1119 stores SO2 as O=S=O; a learner who has seen that form should be told both are in use. Note the McMaster slide says each atom 'has an octet' in O=S=O, which is not correct for S (10 electrons).

conventions.choice: valence electrons - (lone-pair electrons + bonding electrons assigned to the atom); each bond's electrons go wholly to the atom with the higher Pauling electronegativity and are split equally between atoms of the same element. Computed on the single stored Lewis structure.
conventions.why: This is the spec rule (6.3). It reproduces the OpenStax 4.2 guideline results for every species here (H +1, O -2 except -1 in H2O2 and 0 in O2, halogens -1) and sums to the species charge in all 33 files. Resonance-equivalent atoms (the two O of SO2, of a carboxylate, of HCO3-) get the same value whichever resonance form is stored. IUPAC (2016) recommends Allen rather than Pauling electronegativities; for every bond type in this library (C-H, N-H, O-H, C-N, C-O, H-Cl, B-F, S-O, S-F, Xe-F, P-Cl) both scales give the same direction, so the results are identical. No bond in the library joins two different elements with equal Pauling values (the script checks this). Closest pairs among the ten elements: H 2.20 / P 2.19 (0.01), S 2.58 / Xe 2.60 (0.02), C 2.55 / S 2.58 (0.03); none of these pairs is bonded in this library.

conventions.choice: stericNumber = bonded atoms + lone pairs counted on the stored Lewis structure. effectiveStericNumber = the same minus one for an atom covered by the resonance override. Geometry and hybridization are looked up from effectiveStericNumber. Both numbers are given for every atom so the atom card can show either.
conventions.why: Spec 6.3 says the delocalised lone pair "does not count as a domain"; keeping both numbers makes the override visible and testable.

conventions.choice: (bonded atoms, effective lone pairs) -> (2,0) linear; (3,0) trigonal planar; (2,1) bent; (4,0) tetrahedral; (3,1) trigonal pyramidal; (2,2) bent; (5,0) trigonal bipyramidal; (6,0) octahedral; (4,2) square planar. Atoms bonded to fewer than two atoms read "terminal atom". electronGeometry is also given because "bent" covers both the ~120 degree (trigonal planar parent) and ~109.5 degree (tetrahedral parent) cases.
conventions.why: OpenStax 7.6 names ("bent or angular"). Only the combinations that occur in the library are listed; the implementation should add the rest of the table (seesaw, T-shaped, square pyramidal, linear from 5 domains) for completeness.

conventions.choice: Note "one of two equivalent resonance structures; effective order 1.5" on exactly eight bonds: both S-O bonds of SO2; both carboxylate C-O bonds of glycine zwitterion and of alanine zwitterion; the two unprotonated C-O bonds (C1=O1, C1-O2) of HCO3-. Benzene uses the aromatic flag on all six ring bonds instead of a note. NO note on: the C=O / C-OH bonds of acetic acid, neutral glycine, neutral alanine, H2CO3 and the C1-O3 (C-OH) bond of HCO3-; the ester C-O of ethyl acetate; the amide C-N and C=O of acetamide and urea; the O=O bond of O2.
conventions.why: The 1.5 figure is only correct when the two contributing structures are equivalent by symmetry (OpenStax 7.4: the real structure is the average of identical resonance forms). In acids, esters and amides the charge-separated contributor is minor, so the bond orders are not 1.5 and that note text would be wrong. Optional extra, not in the spec: a differently worded note on the amide C-N bonds of acetamide and urea ("partial double-bond character from resonance; rotation restricted") would be accurate and is supported by OpenStax Organic 26.4, but it needs a second note string.

conventions.choice: Computable rule: an atom with at least one lone pair, with no multiple bond of its own, single-bonded to an atom that has a double or triple bond to some other atom. Such an atom is sp2 and one lone pair is not counted as a domain. In this library that selects exactly 14 atoms: SO2 O2 (the single-bonded O-); acetic acid O2 (hydroxyl O); ethyl acetate O2 (ester O); acetamide N1; urea N1 and N2; glycine O2 and alanine O2 (hydroxyl O, neutral forms); glycine zwitterion O2 and alanine zwitterion O2 (carboxylate O-); HCO3- O2 (O-) and O3 (hydroxyl O); H2CO3 O2 and O3 (both hydroxyl O). It does NOT select: amine N of neutral glycine/alanine or methylamine, O of ethanol, any O of glucose, O of H2O2, halogens, ring atoms of benzene.
conventions.why: Conventional status, atom by atom. Amide and urea N (3 atoms): standard in organic chemistry and backed by experiment (planar amide; OpenStax Organic 24.3 and 26.4); the override changes both geometry (trigonal pyramidal -> trigonal planar) and hybridization. Carboxylic, carbonic and ester -O- (8 atoms): sp2 is the organic-chemistry description (LibreTexts Smith 17.6 states it outright); the geometry word stays "bent", only hybridization (sp3 -> sp2) and the parent electron geometry change. TEXTBOOKS DISAGREE HERE: OpenStax Chemistry 2e Example 7.16 (general chemistry) treats the O-H oxygen of glycine as four regions, tetrahedral electron-pair geometry, bent (109 degrees), i.e. sp3; the same example gives the amine N as trigonal pyramidal, which agrees with this table. Terminal O- of carboxylate, HCO3- and SO2 (5 atoms): no geometry is shown; sp2 keeps the two resonance-equivalent oxygens labelled identically, which is the reason to apply the override to them. General chemistry texts rarely assign hybridization to these atoms at all. Verification addendum: an explicit general chemistry statement of the amide N as sp2 / trigonal planar, and of the general rule that an atom whose lone pair is delocalised must be sp2 (or sp), is in the Penn State Chem 110 page (source psu-chem110-delocalized-pi). The disagreement with OpenStax Chemistry 2e Example 7.16 for the carboxylic O-H oxygen stands; the no-override values are stored per atom in withoutResonanceOverride.

conventions.choice: RECOMMENDED rule: geometry is "terminal atom" for every atom bonded to fewer than two atoms. Hybridization: hydrogen -> "none (1s)"; a terminal atom that has a multiple bond or is covered by the resonance override -> from its (effective) steric number (carbonyl O, CO2 O, O2 O, carboxylate/SO2 O- = sp2; N2 N = sp); a terminal atom with only a single bond and no override (in this library only the halogens: F in BF3, SF6, XeF4; Cl in HCl, PCl5) -> "not assigned (terminal atom)". The JSON also carries hybridizationByStericNumberOnly (sp3 for those halogens) so the simpler alternative rule "always use the steric number" can be tested instead if the owner prefers it. NOTE (verification): hybridizationByStericNumberOnly is computed from effectiveStericNumber, i.e. the resonance override is still applied; it differs from hybridization only for the 16 terminal halogens. For the 14 override atoms it reads sp2 although their raw stericNumber is 4. The value with no override at all is given per override atom in withoutResonanceOverride.
conventions.why: A pi bond needs an unhybridized p orbital, so the hybridization of a multiply bonded terminal atom is fixed by the same argument used for central atoms and textbooks do state it (Purdue: sp2 on both C and O of formaldehyde; LibreTexts: carbonyl C and O both sp2). For singly bonded halogens there is no geometric evidence and textbooks split: OpenStax 8.1 describes HCl as overlap of the H 1s with a Cl p orbital (no hybridization), while some courses write sp3 from the steric number (this second half is NOT backed by any fetched source). Showing "sp3" for the F atoms of SF6 would be a claim an instructor could dispute; "not assigned" cannot be wrong.

conventions.choice: Expected strings here are "sp3d (textbook label)" and "sp3d2 (textbook label)" as the task brief states; spec 6.3 words the card text as "sp3d (textbook label; real d-orbital involvement is negligible)". Tests should match on the prefix or the implementation plan should fix one exact string.
conventions.why: OpenStax 8.2 teaches sp3d and sp3d2 (SF6 is its sp3d2 example); the caveat is the spec owner's addition.

conventions.choice: order 1 = 1 sigma; order 2 = 1 sigma + 1 pi; order 3 = 1 sigma + 2 pi, taken from the stored integer order. Aromatic bonds: "1 sigma + delocalised pi (aromatic, effective order 1.5)". Bonds with a resonance note keep the composition of their stored order and show the note.
conventions.why: OpenStax 8.1/8.3: a single bond is a sigma bond, a double bond is one sigma and one pi, a triple bond is one sigma and two pi.

conventions.choice: Lewis file stores O=O with two lone pairs on each O (all electrons paired). The MO record gives two unpaired electrons and bond order 2.
conventions.why: OpenStax 8.4 opens with exactly this discrepancy; spec 6.4 requires the callout.

conventions.choice: Valence levels only (2s- and 2p-derived). The degenerate pi pair is one level with degeneracy 2. Empty antibonding levels are included with electrons 0 so the diagram can draw them. Labels drop the axis subscripts OpenStax uses (sigma2px, pi2py/pi2pz).
conventions.why: Matches spec 5.3 MO diagram shape and OpenStax Figure 8.37 / Table 8.3.

conventions.choice: Labels are element symbol + per-element index (C1, C2, O1, H1 ...), unique within a molecule; heavy atoms first, then hydrogens. Molecule ids are proposed kebab-case names (the project has no molecule registry yet); rename freely, nothing depends on them.
conventions.why: Readable in test tables; the notes field of each molecule says which atom is which.

conventions.choice: build_expected.py recomputes, from the atom and bond lists alone: formal charge per atom and its sum; valence-shell electron count (8, or 2 for H; the only exceptions are B in BF3 = 6, P in PCl5 = 10, S in SF6 = 12, Xe in XeF4 = 12); oxidation state per atom by the Pauling rule and its sum; steric number, override, geometry and hybridization by the rules above; element composition against a hand-written molecular formula; the override atom set against a hand-written list; MO electron totals, bond order, unpaired count and aufbau filling. It refuses to write expected.json on any mismatch.
conventions.why: Spec 6.5 acceptance mirrors these checks.

conventions.choice: Each added entry is computed by build-expected-additions.mjs from the saved PubChem 2D record (or, for a molecule in geometry.json, from its atoms and bonds there) by the conventions of this file as they stood, and by the four that follow. The named cases in src/chem-data/derive.test.ts are the checks written by hand.
conventions.why: One pass, by script, read through atom by atom by its author. There was no second, independent pass of the kind the first 33 structures had, and docs/research/phase-2/README.md says so.

conventions.choice: Every atom of an uncharged species made of one element has oxidation state 0 (H2, Cl2, O2, N2, O3), whatever its Lewis structure. This comes before the rule of convention oxidation-state, and changes one molecule: ozone, whose stored Lewis structure (O=O(+)-O(-)) would give +1 for the central atom, 0 and -1 for the outer two by that rule, which are its formal charges.
conventions.why: The first of the usual rules for oxidation numbers is that an atom of an element is 0, and it is the answer a first-year course expects for ozone. Splitting the electrons of a bond between like atoms leaves each atom with its formal charge, which is zero in H2, O2, N2 and Cl2 and not in ozone; the two outer oxygens of ozone are also equivalent in the real molecule and would be given different values. The derivation in src/chem-data/derive.ts was changed to match on 2026-10-09, with a test.

conventions.topic: Sulfate, phosphate, sulfuric acid, phosphoric acid and sulfur trioxide
conventions.choice: Drawn in the octet-obeying form, as sulfur dioxide is (convention so2-lewis) and by the rule of convention lewis-structures (octet-obeying forms wherever one exists; an expanded valence shell only where unavoidable, as in SF6). Sulfate: four S-O single bonds, S +2, each O -1. Phosphate: four P-O single bonds, P +1, each O -1. Sulfuric acid: S +2, two S-O(-) and two S-OH. Phosphoric acid: P +1, one P-O(-) and three P-OH. Sulfur trioxide: one S=O and two S-O(-), S +2, one of three equivalent resonance structures. PubChem stores each of the five with S=O or P=O double bonds and no formal charge on the central atom.
conventions.why: The same choice as for SO2, for the same reason, so that the library draws one family one way. Oxidation states, steric numbers, geometry and hybridization of the central atom are the same in both drawings (S +6, P +5; tetrahedral, sp3; trigonal planar and sp2 in SO3). Only bond orders, lone pairs and formal charges differ. The competing drawing, which lowers the formal charges by giving the central atom more than eight electrons, is the one the source libretexts-brown-8.7 of this file shows for sulfate beside the octet structure; each of the five molecules carries a note that says both drawings are in use.

conventions.topic: Which added bonds get a resonanceNote
conventions.choice: Note "one of two equivalent resonance structures; effective order 1.5" on both O-O bonds of ozone, the two N-O bonds of nitric acid to the oxygens that carry no hydrogen, both C-O bonds of acetate and of the carboxylate of the serine and cysteine zwitterions. Note "one of three equivalent resonance structures; effective order 1.33" on the three N-O bonds of nitrate, the three C-O bonds of carbonate and the three S-O bonds of sulfur trioxide (4/3: one double and two single bonds shared among three). No note on sulfate, phosphate, sulfuric or phosphoric acid: in the octet form every bond to oxygen is single.
conventions.why: As convention resonance-notes: the figure is right where the contributing structures are equivalent. In nitric acid the two structures are equivalent as drawings but the molecule has no symmetry that makes the two bonds equal: NIST CCCBDB lists 1.211 and 1.199 angstrom for them (experimental geometry page, casno 7697372, read 2026-10-09), and the molecule carries a note that says so.

conventions.choice: The six bonds of every benzene ring: a ring of six carbon atoms drawn with alternating double and single bonds (toluene, phenol, aspirin, acetaminophen, ibuprofen, vanillin, capsaicin, cinnamaldehyde, methyl salicylate, benzaldehyde, dopamine, serotonin, adrenaline, aspartame; both benzene rings of indigo). No other bond is flagged. A ring that holds nitrogen (the pyridine ring of nicotine, the rings of adenine, thymine, caffeine and theobromine, the five-membered ring of serotonin and of indigo) is stored as PubChem draws it, with its double bonds where they are drawn.
conventions.why: The flag says "order 1.5", which is the textbook statement for a benzene ring and is not one for a ring with nitrogen in it or for a fused five-membered ring. A known limit: those rings are aromatic too, and the library does not say so.

conventions.topic: VSEPR geometries added to the vocabulary
conventions.choice: (bonded atoms, lone pairs) -> (4,1) seesaw (SF4); (3,2) T-shaped (ClF3); (2,3) linear (XeF2). Square pyramidal (5,1) stays in the table with no molecule in the library.
conventions.why: Convention geometry-names asked for the rest of the table to be added.

verification.method: Independent script verify-expected/verify.py (written without reference to build_expected.py's logic, using electronegativities fetched fresh from PubChem) recomputed every derived value from the atom and bond lists; every structure was compared with its PubChem 2D SDF record by graph isomorphism; all 21 cited URLs were re-fetched with curl and the cited statements located in the page text (figure content via alt text).

computedChecks.covers: per atom (234): formal charge, valence-shell electron count and octetExceptions list, oxidation state (Pauling rule), bondedAtoms, stericNumber, resonanceOverride (rule re-implemented), effectiveStericNumber, electronGeometry, geometry, hybridization, label/element agreement. Per bond (203): endpoints exist, no duplicates, sigmaPi string, paulingDifference. Per molecule (33): formal charges and oxidation states sum to charge, composition field, composition and net charge and charged-atom set against PubChem, connectivity and bond orders against PubChem. Override atom list (14). MO: electron totals 12 and 10, bond order, unpaired count, aufbau filling, star/type agreement.

pubchemComparison.result: 32 of 33 structures are isomorphic to the PubChem record including bond orders and formal-charge placement. sulfur-dioxide has the same connectivity but PubChem stores O=S=O; this is the documented convention choice, not an error. These CIDs were chosen by the verifier to check structures; they are not part of the original file and alanine's CIDs (5950 L-alanine, 7311724 L-alanine zwitterion) should be re-confirmed when the fetch script is written, as the spec says.

electronegativity.pauling: All ten values match PubChem periodic table and Wikipedia data page.
electronegativity.allen: Fetched from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxidation_state ; same bond direction as Pauling for C-H, N-H, O-H, C-N, C-O, H-Cl, B-F, S-O, S-F, Xe-F, P-Cl.

The paper itself and the Gold Book entry were not readable (De Gruyter returned an empty HTTP 202, Gold Book HTTP 403). Added source wikipedia-oxidation-state.
corrections.evidence: Re-fetched https://iupac.org/recommendation/comprehensive-definition-of-oxidation-state/ : text contains 'ionic approximation' and '88(8), pp. 831-839; doi:10.1515/pac-2015-1204' but no occurrence of 'Allen', 'McArdle' or 'Takats'. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxidation_state contains 'for a simple estimate for the ionic approximation, we can use Allen electronegativities' and the Allen table; my script confirmed Allen and Pauling give the same direction for all 11 heteronuclear bond types in the library.

verification.noChemistryValueChanged: No formal charge, lone-pair count, bond order, oxidation state, steric number, geometry, hybridization or MO value was found wrong. All corrections are to prose, citations, and one field definition.
reviewerConcerns: Carboxylic/ester/carbonic O-H oxygens (8 atoms) shown as sp2 with trigonal-planar electron geometry contradicts the project's own general chemistry text (OpenStax Chemistry 2e Example 7.16: tetrahedral, bent 109 degrees). This is the value most likely to draw an instructor objection. It follows spec 6.3; the owner should decide, and the no-override values are in withoutResonanceOverride.

Terminal O- atoms (5 atoms: SO2 O2, both zwitterion O2, HCO3- O2) and terminal O/N of CO2, O2, N2 are given a hybridization by analogy with formaldehyde O (Purdue) and the carboxylic O (Smith); no fetched source assigns these specific atoms.
SO2: both conventions are in real use (OpenStax octet form; McMaster and PubChem O=S=O). The stored form is defensible and matches the cited text.
MO labels: OpenStax writes the antibonding star after the subscript (sigma 2s*) and keeps axis subscripts (sigma 2px, pi 2py, pi 2pz); the file writes sigma*2s and drops the axes. Notation only.
hypervalent label string differs between the task brief ('sp3d (textbook label)') and spec 6.3 ('sp3d (textbook label; real d-orbital involvement is negligible)'); tests should fix one.
unverifiable: Pauling electronegativities against the CRC Handbook (spec 5.2 names CRC; paywalled). Confirmed only against PubChem and Wikipedia.
IUPAC 2016 recommendation paper and Gold Book entry O04365 themselves (De Gruyter returned empty HTTP 202, Gold Book HTTP 403); the Allen statement is confirmed only via Wikipedia.

Figure content that exists only as images without descriptive alt text: Purdue SO2 resonance figure (formal charges and lone pairs not confirmable; only the surrounding text), Purdue formaldehyde figure, LibreTexts Smith/Morsch figures, OpenStax Figure 8.37 beyond its alt text and caption.
Hybridization label for singly bonded terminal halogens (no source either way beyond OpenStax 8.1's s-p overlap description of HCl).

sp2 label specifically for the ester O of ethyl acetate, the O-H oxygens of H2CO3 and HCO3-, and terminal O- atoms: no source fetched for these species; they follow from the computable rule and the Penn State general statement.
Hybridization of terminal atoms in CO2 (O), O2 (O) and N2 (N): no source fetched that states these; rule-derived.
